messages:
Mia (Customer): Hey team, we just noticed ~12 users who were removed from our IdP are still active in Redwood. From our Okta SCIM logs the deprovision PATCH returns 200, but the users remain in the org and can still access routes. This started after we cleaned up a bunch of group names (replaced slashes and spaces). Can you help?

Hana C: Thanks for flagging, Mia — sorry for the hit. Can you paste one of the SCIM PATCH payloads (redact PII) and the corresponding 200 response? Also confirm whether you use group externalId or displayName for role mapping on your side.

Mia (Customer): Here's an anonymized payload we sent (from Okta webhook):
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "remove",
      "path": "groups[value eq \"00g7abcdEFGHIJklm\"]"
    }
  ]
}
```
and the SCIM endpoint returned:```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "detail": "accepted, deprovision queued",
  "id": "user-1234"
}
```
We do use externalId on groups (we sync externalId = oktaGroup.id). We also have some groups that were renamed in Okta (e.g., from `Engineering/Frontend` to `engineering-frontend`).

okta-bot: Webhook log snippet:
```text
POST /scim/v2/Users/user-1234 HTTP/1.1
Host: scim.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
{ op: 'remove', path: 'groups[value eq "00g7abcdEFGHIJklm"]' }
Response: 200 OK
```

Devon R: Thanks, this looks like a group externalId <> internal normalization mismatch. Quick explainer: the Redwood role-mapper expects the group's `externalId` to match our stored group key. During an earlier migration we started normalizing group displayName -> slug (lowercase, remove punctuation) for a subset of customers — but deprovision webhooks coming from Okta are still referencing the old externalId. If the group was renamed in Okta such that a new externalId was generated, the remove operation will succeed on Okta's side but Redwood won't find a matching group mapping and will queue the deprovision without actually removing the role in our access store.

Hana C: Can you try a manual deprovision from the Redwood admin console and paste the API response (if any)? Also please send the last 4 chars of the SCIM user id (we can match logs).

Mia (Customer): Tried manual remove via console -> got a 403:```json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "message": "cannot modify role mapping: group not found for externalId 00g7abcdEFGHIJklm"
}
```
Last 4 chars of SCIM id: 2345.

Devon R: That 403 confirms it — our API tried to look up the group by externalId and didn't find it. Two remediation paths: 1) temporary compatibility: recreate a group in Okta with the old externalId (not ideal), or 2) run a reconciliation/backfill that maps legacy externalIds to normalized group keys in Redwood and retries pending deprovisions. I can provide a backfill script and DB query to find affected users.

Devon R: Sample query to find pending deprovision entries referencing unknown group externalIds:
```sql
SELECT p.id, p.user_id, p.group_external_id, g.id as resolved_group_id
FROM pending_deprovisions p
LEFT JOIN groups g ON g.external_id = p.group_external_id
WHERE g.id IS NULL
LIMIT 1000;
```
Backfill pseudo-script (dry-run first):
```bash
# find candidate mappings by trying normalized->external lookups
python tools/scim_reconcile.py --dry-run --filter "group_external_id LIKE '00g%' 
"
# sample operation: insert compatibility mapping table mapping.old_external_id -> groups.id
```

Priya S: If we run this in prod please do it as a job on the maintenance lane (throttled). Risk: if there are many queued operations we could hit tokenization/rate limits on downstream services. Suggest we run --dry-run in prod, then run with a small batch window (100 users), monitor error rates. I'll also add a temporary alert to catch retry storms.

Hana C: Mia, are you OK with us performing a reconciliation for your org? We'll need your formal consent to touch user role assignments. We'll also attach the support ticket and provide a rollback plan.

Mia (Customer): Yes please, go ahead. We need those users off access asap. We approve reconciliation and any transient compatibility mappings — we'll revoke after the clean up. Ticket: CS-4521.

Sam E: Eng-runtime here — I'll own the job. Plan: 1) run reconcile dry-run (find affected ~18 users), 2) run small-batch reconcile to create compatibility mappings and retry pending deprovisions, 3) validate that users are removed and delete compat mappings. ETA for dry-run: 30m, full run if clean: 2h.

Devon R: Command I'll run (internal):
```bash
# dry-run
./bin/scim-reconcile --org-id=org-9876 --dry-run --limit=200
# apply (throttled)
./bin/scim-reconcile --org-id=org-9876 --apply --batch-size=50 --sleep=2
```
Note: the tool records ops in audit logs and emits a report.

Priya S: Kicking off on maintenance lane now. Monitor: scim.reconcile.failures and access.assignments.delta. I'll pause other SCIM jobs until this stabilizes.

[~2 hours later]

Devon R: Backfill finished. Results summary: 18 pending deprovisions retried, 18 users deprovisioned successfully, created 18 temporary compatibility mappings (old_external_id -> group_id) which will be removed in 24h. No errors above the threshold. Audit report: /reports/scim_reconcile/CS-4521-1859004321.csv.

Hana C: Mia, can you verify those users are removed on your end and confirm there's no one still seeing access?

Mia (Customer): Confirmed, users are removed and apps no longer accessible. Thank you! :white_check_mark: Also appreciated the dry-run and the step throttling.

Sam E: I'll schedule the cleanup job to remove the compatibility mappings in 24h and keep monitoring for 48h. Leaving P2 ticket open for follow-up.

Hana C: Closing loop on CS side — filing a short postmortem with recommended product fix: unify group lookup to accept both legacy externalId and normalized keys at deprovision time, and add a migrations dashboard so customers know when group externalIds change.

Devon R: Agreed — I'll add the PR with safer lookup logic and an e2e test that simulates group renames.

Mia (Customer): Thank you all, huge help.
